Diego,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As part of our procurement for the next phase of our patient-data routing project, Procurement and Security have requested a completed HIPAA readiness questionnaire and a draft BAA we can circulate internally. Attached is MedSyn's standard questionnaire (MedSyn_HIPAA_Questionnaire_2025.xlsx) and a short risk register template we use for scoring controls. Can you confirm the following for our review: 

- Whether Redwood can sign our standard BAA or if you provide a counter-draft (preferred to see a Redwood draft)
- Clarify PHI handling for hosted vs. Private deployments (KV cache persistence, telemetry, logs)
- Encryption: at-rest encryption details and KMS/HSM support
- Evidence we can share with auditors (SOC 2 type II report, pen test summary, recent vulnerability scan reports)

Our timeline: initial vendor packet due by Dec 5, procurement committee meets Dec 10. If you can return the questionnaire and a BAA draft by Nov 28 that would be ideal.

Best,
Alice

Alice —

Thanks for the clear list and the questionnaire. We're happy to move quickly on this. Quick summary of what we'll provide by Nov 28: 

- Completed questionnaire (see attached: Redwood_HIPAA_Q_Responses_20251126.pdf)
- Redwood draft BAA (we'll attach a redline-friendly Word doc to the next thread: Redwood_BAA_Draft_v2.docx)
- Copies of non-sensitive artifacts: SOC 2 Type II summary + pen test executive summary (we can provide a redacted package for procurement use)

Short answers to your bullets: 
- BAA: Redwood typically provides a draft BAA that mirrors our operational model; we can accept reasonable MedSyn redlines but will need to escalate a few clauses to legal (data residency, subcontractor disclosure, indemnity limits).
- PHI handling: For hosted customers who process PHI we offer a Dedicated or Private deployment option. PHI in Hosted flows is kept in isolated namespaces; we employ automatic KV cache eviction and prefix caching controls. Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) give you persistent control of storage and keys.
- Encryption: AES-256 at rest; we support customer-supplied KMS keys via our KMS integrations and can sign an HSM-backed key access addendum for Dedicated customers.
- Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted) and pen test exec summary are available; full reports require an NDA.

Next steps: 
1) I'll attach the Redwood_BAA_Draft_v2.docx and our completed questionnaire in a follow-up.
2) Can you confirm whether MedSyn requires E2E key custody (you manage keys) or are you okay with Redwood-managed customer keys? That affects a few BAA clauses.
3) If procurement wants a short 30-min technical call for Security to walk the architecture, we can schedule with our security lead (Rachel).

Thanks — aiming to get docs over later today.

— Diego

Diego,

Received, thanks — the responses look good at a glance. A couple clarifying items from Security that will affect procurement scoring: 

- Data residency: MedSyn requires PHI to stay in US regions for this project. Can you confirm Redwood will pin the model and storage to a US region for Dedicated/Hosted?
- Key custody: We prefer customer-controlled keys (KMS) for Dedicated. Does your Dedicated offering support BYOK and HSM-backed KMS?
- Logging/audit: We need log export that includes token-level request IDs and payload metadata (redacted) for 7 years. Is that configurable?

Attached our small risk register with a couple of control questions filled in (MedSyn_Risk_Register.xlsx). Procurement would like to lock vendor packets by Dec 5; if you think any of the asked items need legal redlines, note them in the BAA draft.

Also: procurement asked whether Redwood will accept limited liability carve-outs tied to data incidents — we'll expect to see your stance in the BAA.

Best,
Alice

Diego / Rachel —

Thanks for the heads up. I reviewed the draft BAA and the likely redlines. High-level direction: 

- Liability: we should be willing to accept a limited liability carve-out tied to gross negligence or willful misconduct, but not unlimited PHI liability. Propose cap at contract value for this project with carve-outs for willful misconduct.
- KMS/HSM: Accept customer-managed KMS for Dedicated with an addendum specifying KMS configuration and key rotation responsibilities. Rachel — confirm support for HSM-backed keys; if it's not available as-standard we can offer as an add-on (pricing and a short SLA).
- Audit logs/retention: Approve option to extend retention to 7 years as a paid retention tier. Rachel, we need a bullet list of expected storage delta + estimated monthly cost for the procurement packet.
- Subprocessors: Rather than quarterly full lists, propose a quarterly notice of material changes plus a right-to-audit with 30 days' notice for high-risk subprocessors.

If Security confirms HSM/BYOK and the cost delta for 7-year retention, I think we can accept MedSyn's asks with those commercial guardrails. I'll prepare a 'redline-ready' comment set for the BAA and Diego you can return to MedSyn.

— Lauren
